section_summary: This section documents United States, Allied, and Japanese policies and negotiations concerning the revival of Japan's merchant marine and shipbuilding industry between 1946 and 1949. It covers diplomatic exchanges within the Far Eastern Commission and State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee on Japanese shipping levels, British security objections to Japanese export shipbuilding countered by American economic recovery arguments, and Soviet requests for wooden vessel construction. Later records detail SCAP export shipbuilding programs and foreign contracts with Danish, Norwegian, American, and Philippine companies, including cargo ships built in Nagasaki for the De La Rama Steamship Company.

subfiles.about: Transmits an interim reply from SCAP regarding shipbuilding and merchant shipping.
subfiles.from: A. D. Reid, Secretary, SWNCC
subfiles.summary: Forwards SCAP's interim reply stating action is pending on the FEC consultative message regarding shipbuilding.
subfiles.title: SWN-4713: Communication from Chairman Pro Tempore of Far Eastern Commission for Transmittal to SCAP

subfiles.about: Relays SCAP's interim reply concerning shipbuilding and merchant shipping to the FEC.
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Informs the Far Eastern Commission that SCAP reported action is pending on shipbuilding consultations.
subfiles.title: Consultative Message to SCAP Regarding Shipbuilding and Merchant Shipping

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP's follow-up message requesting study time on shipping questions.
subfiles.from: A. D. Reid, Secretary, SWNCC
subfiles.summary: Reports SCAP requires study on shipping queries, estimating a reply by September 30.
subfiles.title: SWN-4750: Communication from Chairman Pro Tempore of Far Eastern Commission for Transmittal to SCAP

subfiles.about: Informs the FEC of SCAP's estimated reply date on shipbuilding matters.
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Advises the Far Eastern Commission that SCAP expects to reply on shipbuilding by September 30.
subfiles.title: Consultative Message to SCAP Regarding Shipbuilding and Merchant Shipping

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP's substantive reply concerning Japanese shipping and shipyard capacity.
subfiles.from: H. W. Moseley, Secretary, SWNCC
subfiles.summary: Forwards SCAP's substantive reply regarding Japanese shipbuilding and merchant shipping for transmittal to the FEC.
subfiles.title: SWN-4891: Communication from Chairman Pro Tempore of Far Eastern Commission for Transmittal to SCAP

subfiles.about: Provides detailed statistics on Japanese shipping requirements, operable fleet, and shipyard capacity.
subfiles.from: GHQ SCAP Tokyo Japan
subfiles.summary: Details Japanese tonnage needs for repatriation and trade, operable fleet estimates through 1947, and shipyard capacities.
subfiles.title: Radio Message C 67048 on Japanese Merchant Shipping and Shipbuilding Capacity
subfiles.to: War Department for Joint Chiefs of Staff

subfiles.about: Transmits correspondence concerning proposed Soviet procurement of Japanese wooden vessels.
subfiles.from: George A. Abbey, Counselor of Mission in Charge, USPOLAD Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits letters between the Soviet Allied Council member and SCAP ESS regarding wooden vessel construction.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 860: Wooden Vessels to be Constructed by the Japanese Government for the U.S.S.R.

subfiles.about: Inquires about constructing wooden tugs, fishing vessels, and lighters in Japan for the USSR.
subfiles.from: A. O. Lvov, Acting Economic Adviser to USSR Member, Allied Council for Japan
subfiles.summary: Requests information on how many wooden tugs, fishing vessels, and lighters Japan could construct by June 1947.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Concerning Japanese Construction of Wooden Vessels for the U.S.S.R.
subfiles.to: Brig. General W. F. Marquat, Chief, ESS, GHQ SCAP

subfiles.about: Proposes delivery schedules for wooden tugboats and barges in exchange for Soviet raw materials.
subfiles.from: F. D. Pickelle, Deputy Chief, Foreign Trade Division, ESS, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Outlines delivery schedules for wooden tugs and barges in exchange for Soviet coal, pulp, and crude oil.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Wooden Vessels
subfiles.to: A. O. Lvov, Member for USSR, Allied Council for Japan

subfiles.about: Discusses policy revisions on Japanese shipping and drydock limits approved by SWNCC.
subfiles.from: OE - Mr. Whitman
subfiles.summary: Recommends handling Japanese shipping policy separately in SWNCC to avoid delaying the general level-of-industry paper.
subfiles.title: Control of Japanese Shipping and Merchant Shipbuilding

subfiles.about: Submits a draft reply to the Army Department concerning staff studies on Japanese shipping.
subfiles.from: R. A. Fearey (FE:NA)
subfiles.summary: Presents a proposed letter to Mr. West outlining State Department views on Japanese shipbuilding recommendations.
subfiles.title: Japanese Shipping and Shipbuilding

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP's November 8 message regarding Japanese shipping and shipyards to the FEC.
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Forwards SCAP's detailed statistical message on Japanese shipping requirements to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.title: Consultative Message on Japanese Shipbuilding and Merchant Shipping

subfiles.about: Enumerates Japanese merchant fleet tonnages and shipyard facilities.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Lists Japanese tonnage requirements for coastal trade and repatriation, along with operable fleet and shipyard estimates.
subfiles.title: Message on Japanese Shipping Requirements and Operating Fleet

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP's November 8 report on Japanese merchant shipping.
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Duplicate memorandum transmitting SCAP's November 8 message on shipbuilding and shipping to the FEC.
subfiles.title: Consultative Message on Japanese Shipbuilding and Merchant Shipping (Duplicate Copy)

subfiles.about: Records British representations regarding security concerns over Japanese shipbuilding for export.
subfiles.from: J. M. Allison, Chief, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs
subfiles.summary: Records British Counselor Graves presenting security objections to Japanese export shipbuilding, with US Navy rebuttal noted.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Japanese Building of Merchant Ships for Export

subfiles.about: Sets forth British objections to permitting Japanese shipyards to build merchant ships for export.
subfiles.from: British Embassy, Washington, D.C.
subfiles.summary: Expresses British concern that export shipbuilding creates a dangerous Japanese maritime and labor reserve exceeding peaceful requirements.
subfiles.title: Aide-Mémoire on Japanese Shipbuilding Capacity and Export Construction

subfiles.about: Replies to British representations, justifying SCAP authorization of Japanese export shipbuilding.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: Defends Japanese construction of export vessels to improve foreign exchange and ease the global tanker shortage. Denies any security threat, noting labor is prewar and shipyard capacity remains subject to reparations.
subfiles.title: Aide-Mémoire in Reply to British Embassy on Japanese Shipbuilding for Export

subfiles.about: Reports Italian shipbuilders' claims regarding low Japanese price quotations for tankers.
subfiles.from: James Clement Dunn, American Embassy, Rome
subfiles.summary: Reports Italian shipbuilders' claims that Japanese yards offer tankers at prices ten percent below Scandinavian rates.
subfiles.title: Telegram 2627 from Rome: Japanese Tanker Construction Quotations

subfiles.about: Clarifies Japanese tanker negotiations and refutes reports of undercutting Scandinavian prices.
subfiles.from: SCAP (relayed via Seoul)
subfiles.summary: SCAP clarifies that export ship negotiations involve standard American payment terms with no quoted prices yet.
subfiles.title: Telegram 135 from Seoul: Clarification of Japanese Tanker Construction

subfiles.about: Quotes news reports on SCAP allowing general repair and conversion of foreign vessels.
subfiles.from: American Consulate General, Shanghai
subfiles.summary: Reports Central News Agency story on SCAP permitting Japanese shipyards to perform general foreign ship repairs.
subfiles.title: Telegram 1844 from Shanghai: New Policy on Foreign Ship Repair in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP press release authorizing foreign vessel repair and conversion in Japanese yards.
subfiles.from: W. H. Lawrence Jr., Acting Political Adviser, USPOLAD Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits SCAP press release stating foreign ship repairs will utilize idle capacity and maintain skilled shipyard labor.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 565: Announcement of New Policy on Foreign Ship Repair

subfiles.about: Transmits Maritime Commission report on the 1948 Japanese shipbuilding program.
subfiles.from: A. C. Fleming, Consul General, Shanghai
subfiles.summary: Transmits a report from the Yokohama office of the US Maritime Commission regarding Japanese shipbuilding.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 895: Shipbuilding in Japan

subfiles.about: Details domestic construction quarterly programs and foreign export orders in Japanese shipyards.
subfiles.from: Yokohama Office, United States Maritime Commission
subfiles.summary: Outlines SCAP's 1948 domestic shipbuilding program, export contracts for five nations, and steel mill production.
subfiles.title: SCAP Program for Ship Building

subfiles.about: Briefs Assistant Secretary of Labor Gibson on NSC proposals concerning Japanese shipbuilding capacity.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Records conference briefing Labor Assistant Secretary Gibson on the Japanese shipbuilding reparations proposal before the NSC.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Japanese Shipbuilding Capacity and Reparations

subfiles.about: Provides details on SCAP's tentative fifteen-ship export program and foreign company interest.
subfiles.from: Garrison Norton, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Informs the Maritime Commission of SCAP's tentative fifteen-ship export program for US, Philippine, French, Danish, and Norwegian interests.
subfiles.title: Letter to Huntington T. Morse Concerning Export Shipbuilding Program in Japan
subfiles.to: Huntington T. Morse, US Maritime Commission

subfiles.about: Reports signing of contracts for two steel ships built in Japan for Denmark.
subfiles.from: Huston, USPOLAD Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports contracts signed for an 18,000-ton tanker at Harima and a 10,000-ton cargo ship at Mitsubishi for Denmark.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-110: Export Ship Contracts for Danish East Asiatic Company

subfiles.about: Analyzes legal restrictions impacting Japanese shipping and US occupation costs.
subfiles.from: R. A. Fearey (FE:NA)
subfiles.summary: Discusses legislative obstacles to reducing occupation costs, specifically Public Law 423 regarding surplus vessels and the 1904 cargo law.
subfiles.title: Japanese Shipping and Shipbuilding Legislation

subfiles.about: Refers Ingalls Shipbuilding Corporation's inquiry on Japanese shipbuilding to the Army Department.
subfiles.from: Walter A. Radius, Director, Office of Transport and Communications
subfiles.summary: Refers Ingalls Shipbuilding Corporation's inquiry regarding the Japanese shipbuilding program to the Department of the Army.
subfiles.title: Letter to Monro B. Lanier Concerning Japanese Shipbuilding Inquiry
subfiles.to: Monro B. Lanier, President, Ingalls Shipbuilding Corporation

subfiles.about: Inquires about Japanese shipbuilding orders and proposes converting military-type vessels in American yards.
subfiles.from: Monro B. Lanier, President, The Ingalls Shipbuilding Corporation
subfiles.summary: Inquires about Japanese shipbuilding contracts and proposes converting surplus military vessels in US yards at lower costs.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Japanese Shipbuilding Program and Conversion Opportunities
subfiles.to: Export License Division, Department of State (Attn: Mr. Pomeroy)

subfiles.about: Acknowledges referral of company inquiry to the Department of the Army.
subfiles.from: Monro B. Lanier, President, The Ingalls Shipbuilding Corporation
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt of Radius's letter confirming referral of Ingalls' shipbuilding inquiry to the Department of the Army.
subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Referral on Japanese Shipbuilding Inquiry
subfiles.to: Walter A. Radius, Director, Office of Transport and Communications

subfiles.about: Transmits newspaper photograph of cargo vessel under construction in Nagasaki for Philippine company.
subfiles.from: R. R. Spence, American Embassy, Manila
subfiles.summary: Transmits press photograph of a 10,000-ton cargo vessel under construction in Nagasaki for De La Rama Steamship Company.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 841: Construction of New Vessel

subfiles.about: Depicts construction of a 10,000-ton cargo ship in Nagasaki for De La Rama Steamship Company.
subfiles.from: The Evening News, Manila
subfiles.summary: Photograph depicting construction of one of three 10,000-ton vessels at Mitsubishi Nagasaki for the National Development Company.
subfiles.title: Newspaper Photograph: Vessel Construction at Mitsubishi Nagasaki Yard

subfiles.about: Transmits newspaper article on De La Rama Steamship Company elections and Japanese shipbuilding program.
subfiles.from: R. R. Spence, Maritime Attaché, American Embassy, Manila
subfiles.summary: Transmits clipping from Manila Times detailing election of De La Rama officers and schedules for ships built in Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1037: Election of De La Rama Steamship Company Officials

subfiles.from: The Manila Times

subfiles.title: Osmeña Re-Elected De La Rama Head, Pedrosa Remains Board Chairman
